intro: An optimizer suddenly takes a huge step. The supplied patch caps each coordinate, but that can rotate the overall update. Repair it so all parameter tensors share one scaling factor.
task: Return a dictionary with norm (the original global L2 norm) and grads (a list of NumPy arrays). Scale every tensor by min(1, max_norm / norm), using scale one when norm is zero.
requirements: grads is a nonempty Python list of nonempty numeric arrays, each with at least one axis. Their shapes may differ.
Treat all entries across the list as one concatenated vector when computing the L2 norm. Do not clip each tensor independently.
max_norm is a finite nonnegative scalar. Reject malformed inputs and non-finite values with ValueError. Checks use magnitudes up to 1e6.
Return the original norm before clipping. Preserve shapes, do not mutate inputs, and return new arrays even when no clipping is needed.

hints.title: Spot the rotation
hints.body: Coordinate clipping turns [3,4] into [2,2] at limit 2. Those vectors do not point in the same direction.

hints.title: One norm across parameters
hints.body: Add the squared entries from every tensor, then take one square root.

hints.title: Do not amplify
hints.body: Cap the multiplier at one. When norm is zero, avoid division and keep the zero arrays.

explanation: Global norm clipping changes the update's length while preserving its direction. It multiplies every coordinate of every gradient tensor by the same nonnegative factor.

Clipping each tensor separately changes the relative contribution of different parameter groups. Clipping individual coordinates can also rotate the update; neither operation is this lesson's contract.
Returning the norm before clipping lets an experiment record when clipping activated. A small returned clipped norm alone would hide how large the original gradient was.

Run the flawed starter on the first example and compare coordinate ratios before and after. Clipping can limit a single step, but it does not repair an incorrect derivative or guarantee stable training.
